Summary: M365 Hardening Kit: Identity & access (Entra ID)
M365 Hardening Kit: Exchange Online & email security

Description:
Why: If Conditional Access or MFA is misconfigured you can lock every admin out of the tenant. Two cloud-only emergency accounts keep a way back in.

Steps:
# Create two cloud-only accounts on the *.onmicrosoft.com domain with the Global Administrator role.
# Give them long random passwords or FIDO2 keys stored in two separate secure locations.
# Exclude both accounts from every Conditional Access policy.
# Create an alert for any sign-in by these accounts.

Verify: Both accounts exist, are excluded from all CA policies and a sign-in alert fires on a test sign-in.
Licence: Any
Effort: 30 min

Why: Most account takeovers start with a stolen or sprayed password. MFA blocks the large majority of them.

Steps:
# No Entra ID P1: turn on Security defaults (Entra admin center > Overview > Properties > Manage security defaults).
# With Entra ID P1: create a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for all users and all cloud apps, excluding the break-glass accounts.
# Start in Report-only mode for a few days, check sign-in logs, then switch to On.
# Require phishing-resistant MFA for admin roles where possible.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-MgPolicyIdentitySecurityDefaultEnforcementPolicy | Select-Object IsEnabled; Get-MgIdentityConditionalAccessPolicy | Select-Object DisplayName, State
{code}

Verify: Sign-in logs show MFA satisfied for interactive sign-ins; no user is excluded except break-glass accounts.
Licence: Free (Security defaults) or Entra ID P1 (Conditional Access)
Effort: 1-2 h

Why: Legacy protocols (basic auth over IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH, older Office clients) cannot do MFA and are the main path for password-spray attacks.

Steps:
# Check Entra sign-in logs filtered by Client app = legacy clients to find who still uses them.
# Create a Conditional Access policy: all users, all cloud apps, client apps = Exchange ActiveSync + Other clients, grant = Block (exclude break-glass).
# Run in Report-only first, fix remaining users, then turn On.
# Disable SMTP AUTH at the organisation level unless a device really needs it.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-TransportConfig | Select-Object SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled
{code}

Verify: No successful legacy-auth sign-ins in the last 7 days.
Licence: Entra ID P1 (or Security defaults)
Effort: 1 h

Why: Every Global Administrator is a full-tenant compromise if phished. Daily mail use on an admin account multiplies the risk.

Steps:
# List all users with privileged roles (Entra admin center > Roles and administrators).
# Keep 2-4 Global Administrators; move others to least-privilege roles (e.g. Exchange or User Administrator).
# Use separate cloud-only admin accounts with no mailbox for admin work.
# With Entra ID P2, make roles eligible through Privileged Identity Management (PIM).

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId (Get-MgDirectoryRole -Filter "displayName eq 'Global Administrator'").Id | ForEach-Object { $_.AdditionalProperties.userPrincipalName }
{code}

Verify: 2-4 Global Admins, all cloud-only, none used for daily email.
Licence: Any (PIM needs Entra ID P2)
Effort: 1-2 h

Why: Consent-phishing apps get mailbox and file access without a password. Unrestricted user consent lets any user grant it.

Steps:
# Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions.
# Allow user consent only for apps from verified publishers for low-impact permissions, or disable user consent.
# Turn on the admin consent workflow so users can request access.
# Review existing app grants for unexpected high-privilege permissions.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-MgPolicyAuthorizationPolicy | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DefaultUserRolePermissions | Select-Object PermissionGrantPoliciesAssigned
{code}

Verify: User consent setting is restricted and the admin consent workflow is on.
Licence: Any
Effort: 30 min

Why: Without the unified audit log there is no evidence to investigate an incident.

Steps:
# Microsoft Purview portal > Audit: confirm auditing is on (start recording if prompted).
# Confirm mailbox auditing is enabled by default for the organisation.
# Note your audit retention period for your license.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Select-Object UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled; Get-OrganizationConfig | Select-Object AuditDisabled
{code}

Verify: An audit search returns events from the last 24 hours.
Licence: Any (retention depends on license)
Effort: 15 min

Why: Attackers who take over a mailbox add forwarding rules to copy mail out silently.

Steps:
# Microsoft Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies > Anti-spam > Outbound policy.
# Set automatic forwarding to Off for everyone; create a scoped exception policy only for approved mailboxes.
# Review existing inbox rules and mailbox forwarding for external addresses.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy | Select-Object Name, AutoForwardingMode; Get-EXOMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited -Properties ForwardingSmtpAddress | Where-Object { $_.ForwardingSmtpAddress } | Select-Object Name, ForwardingSmtpAddress
{code}

Verify: A test inbox rule forwarding to an external address is blocked; no unapproved forwarding remains.
Licence: Exchange Online
Effort: 30 min

Summary: [E08] Apply the Standard preset security policy
Description:
Why: Microsoft's preset policies apply recommended anti-phishing, anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments settings in one step and update with new recommendations.

Steps:
# Microsoft Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies > Preset security policies.
# Turn on Standard protection for all recipients (Strict for executives and finance if you can).
# With Defender for Office 365, Safe Links and Safe Attachments are included.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-EOPProtectionPolicyRule | Select-Object Name, State
{code}

Verify: Preset policy shows On and covers all recipients.
Licence: EOP (Defender for Office 365 for Safe Links/Attachments)
Effort: 30 min

Summary: [E09] Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC
Description:
Why: Without email authentication anyone can send mail that appears to come from your domain.

Steps:
# Publish one SPF record listing every service that sends as your domain.
# Enable DKIM signing for each custom domain in the Defender portal and publish the two CNAME records.
# Publish DMARC with p=none and a reporting address, review reports for 2-4 weeks, then move to quarantine.

Check (read-only):
{code:powershell}
Get-DkimSigningConfig | Select-Object Domain, Enabled
{code}

Verify: A message header shows spf=pass, dkim=pass, dmarc=pass.
Licence: Any
Effort: 1 h + DNS wait

Summary: [E10] Self-service password reset with banned passwords
Description:
Why: SSPR cuts helpdesk-assisted resets (a social-engineering target) and banned-password lists stop the most guessed passwords.

Steps:
# Entra admin center > Protection > Password reset: enable for all users with two methods.
# Use combined security-info registration so users register MFA and SSPR together.
# Add your company and product names to the custom banned password list (Entra Password Protection).

Verify: A test user can reset a password with two methods; a banned password is rejected.
Licence: Entra ID P1 for SSPR with on-prem writeback and custom banned list
Effort: 1 h
